VBO:0200031.summary: Happy and alert, the American Brittany brings an energetic, eager manner to this pointing-dog tradition. American keepers maintain the breed for field work as well as showing. At Frosty Meadows, retired female Bella completed obedience training and won class awards; Cooper, who lived to twelve, was the first dog loaded for family hunting trips.
VBO:0200031.shortDescription: A happy, alert American pointing dog, with keeper accounts of obedience-class awards and a place on family hunting trips.

sources.title: Continental Kennel Club: American and French Brittany varieties
sources.evidence: Entire actual substantive standard/history/temperament body read. Explicit two varieties same breed; American larger range/leggier somewhat lighter compact frame versus French measured proportions. Both literal full natural medium tail reaching hock, straight/gently curved, highset carried horizontal/slightly lower preferred; bob/dock also acknowledged. Ordinary leg/compact paw anatomy, short triangular folded ears and moderate dense flat/wavy coat. Shared energetic/eager learning tendency, not unique temperament caused by American label; all clinical/safety/suitability/ancestor speculation and numerical breed ratings excluded.
